simple.summary: נָכַל (nâkal) means to defraud , i.e. act treacherously First listed occurrence: Gen 37 18.

definitions.full: H5230. nakal [ נָכַל ] verb be crafty, deceitful, knavish (Assyrian nakâlu, be crafty, cunning; נְכֵל ᵑ7 be crafty , Pa`el deceive ; Syriac deceive, plot ; compare perhaps act faithlessly , faithless , Prä Amhar. Spr. 90 ); — Qal Participle נוֺכֵל Mal 1:14 knave . Pi`el Perfect 3masculine plural with accusative of congnate meaning with verb לָכֶם נִכְּלוּ אֲשֶׁר נִכְלֵיהֶם Num 25:18 their wiles with which they beguiled you . Hithpa`el Imperfect לַהֲמִיתוֺ אֹתוֺ וַיִּתְנַכְּלוּ Gen 37:18 they knavishly planned against him (Kö iii. 9 ), etc.; Infinitive construct בְ לְחִתְנַכֵּל Psa 105:25 to deal knavishly with .
